title: Design a Code Assistant
summary: Two products behind one name: inline completion that must answer in a couple of hundred milliseconds, and a repository-aware chat that can take seconds. We size both, assemble context from the repo, use fill-in-the-middle, and plan evaluation.
objectives: Estimate request rates, tokens, cost and GPUs for inline completion and chat separately, with workday-concentrated traffic
Assemble a token-budgeted context from the current file, its neighbours and a repository index
Explain fill-in-the-middle prompting and how a completion knows where to stop
Build a latency budget for inline completion and contrast it with chat
Plan offline (pass@k) and online (acceptance, retention) evaluation and the main safety risks
prerequisites: Work through [A Framework for LLM System Design](/learn/llm-system-design/design-framework) first. It helps to know [TTFT and TPOT](/learn/inference-and-serving/measuring-inference), [prefix caching](/learn/inference-and-serving/caching) and [embedding retrieval](/learn/retrieval-and-rag/sparse-and-dense).
